{{Short description|Statistical oversampling method}}
{{Technical|date=July 2025}}
In statistics, '''synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE)''' is a method for [[Oversampling and undersampling in data analysis|oversampling]] samples when dealing with imbalanced classification categories within a dataset. The problem with doing statistical inference and modelling on imbalanced datasets is that the inferences and results from those analyses will be biased towards the majority class. Other solutions undersample the majority class to be equivalently represented in the data with the minority class. Instead of undersampling the majority class, SMOTE oversamples the minority class.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Chawla |first1=N. V. |title=SMOTE: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique |date=2011-06-09 |last2=Bowyer |first2=K. W. |last3=Hall |first3=L. O. |last4=Kegelmeyer |first4=W. P. |journal=Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research |volume=16 |pages=321–357 |doi=10.1613/jair.953 |doi-access=free |arxiv=1106.1813 }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Chawla |first1=N. V. |last2=Bowyer |first2=K. W. |last3=Hall |first3=L. O. |last4=Kegelmeyer |first4=W. P. |date=2002-06-01 |title=SMOTE: Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique |url=https://www.jair.org/index.php/jair/article/view/10302 |journal=Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research |language=en |volume=16 |pages=321–357 |doi=10.1613/jair.953  |doi-access=free|issn=1076-9757|arxiv=1106.1813 }}</ref> However, this technique has been shown to yield poorly calibrated models, with an overestimated probability to belong to the minority class.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=van den Goorbergh|first1=Ruben|last2=van Smeden|first2=Maarten|last3=Timmerman|first3=Dirk|last4=Van Calster|first4=Ben|date=2022-09-01|title=The harm of class imbalance corrections for risk prediction models: illustration and simulation using logistic regression |url=https://academic.oup.com/jamia/article/29/9/1525/6605096?login=false|journal=Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association |language=en|volume=29|issue=9|pages=1525–1534 |doi=10.1093/jamia/ocac093|pmid=35686364 |pmc=9382395 |issn=1527-974X}}</ref>

== Limitations ==
SMOTE does come with some limitations and challenges:<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Alkhawaldeh |first1=Ibraheem M. |last2=Albalkhi |first2=Ibrahem |last3=Naswhan |first3=Abdulqadir Jeprel |date=2023-12-20 |title=Challenges and limitations of synthetic minority oversampling techniques in machine learning |journal=World Journal of Methodology |language=en |volume=13 |issue=5 |pages=373–378 |doi=10.5662/wjm.v13.i5.373 |pmid=38229946 |doi-access=free |pmc=10789107}}</ref>

* [[Overfitting]] during the training process
* Favorable outcomes in the machine learning process, but questionable translation to practical uses
* Synthetically created sample may belong to a different class
* Synthetic data may not match the original distribution of the minority class

== Variations ==
Two variations to the SMOTE algorithm were proposed in the initial SMOTE paper:<ref name=":0" />

* SMOTE-NC: applies to datasets with a mix of [[Nominal data|nominal]] and [[continuous data]]
* SMOTE-N: accounts for nominal features, with the nearest neighbors algorithm being computed using the modified version of Value Difference Metric (VDM), which looks at the overlap of feature values over all feature vectors

Other variations include:<ref>{{Cite web |title=Over-sampling methods — Version 0.13.0 |url=https://imbalanced-learn.org/stable/references/over_sampling.html |access-date=2025-07-16 |website=imbalanced-learn.org}}</ref>

* ADASYN: use a weighted distribution for different minority class examples according to their level of difficulty in learning<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Elreedy |first1=Dina |last2=Atiya |first2=Amir F. |date=2019-12-01 |title=A Comprehensive Analysis of Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) for handling class imbalance |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0020025519306838 |journal=Information Sciences |volume=505 |pages=32–64 |doi=10.1016/j.ins.2019.07.070 |issn=0020-0255|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=He |first1=Haibo |last2=Bai |first2=Yang |last3=Garcia |first3=Edwardo A. |last4=Li |first4=Shutao |chapter=ADASYN: Adaptive synthetic sampling approach for imbalanced learning |date=2008-06-01 |title=2008 IEEE International Joint Conference on Neural Networks (IEEE World Congress on Computational Intelligence) |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1109/ijcnn.2008.4633969 |publisher=[[IEEE]] |pages=1322–1328 |doi=10.1109/ijcnn.2008.4633969 |isbn=978-1-4244-1820-6 }}</ref>
* Borderline-SMOTE: only the minority examples near the borderline are over-sampled<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Han |first1=Hui |last2=Wang |first2=Wen-Yuan |last3=Mao |first3=Bing-Huan |chapter=Borderline-SMOTE: A New Over-Sampling Method in Imbalanced Data Sets Learning |date=2005-08-23 |title=Advances in Intelligent Computing |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/11538059_91 |journal=Proceedings of the 2005 International Conference on Advances in Intelligent Computing - Volume Part I |series=ICIC'05 |location=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer-Verlag |volume=Part I |pages=878–887 |doi=10.1007/11538059_91 |isbn=978-3-540-28226-6}}</ref>
* SMOTE-Tomek: applying Tomek links to the oversampled training set as a data cleaning step to remove samples overlapping the category boundaries<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Batista |first1=Gustavo E. A. P. A. |last2=Prati |first2=Ronaldo C. |last3=Monard |first3=Maria Carolina |date=2004-06-01 |title=A study of the behavior of several methods for balancing machine learning training data |url=https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/1007730.1007735 |journal=SIGKDD Explor. Newsl. |volume=6 |issue=1 |pages=20–29 |doi=10.1145/1007730.1007735 |issn=1931-0145|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* SMOTE-ENN: uses the Edited Nearest Neighbor Rule, which removes any example whose class label differs from the class of at least two of its three nearest neighbors<ref name=":2" />

== Algorithm ==
The SMOTE algorithm can be abstracted with the following [[pseudocode]]:<ref name=":0" />

<syntaxhighlight lang="text" line="1">
if N < 100; then
    Randomize the T minority class samples
    T = (N/100) ∗ T
    N = 100
endif

N = (int)(N/100)
k = Number of nearest neighbors
numattrs = Number of attributes
Sample[ ][ ]: array for original minority class samples
newindex: keeps a count of number of synthetic samples generated, initialized to 0
Synthetic[ ][ ]: array for synthetic samples

for i <- 1 to T
    Compute k nearest neighbors for i, and save the indices in the nnarray
    Populate(N , i, nnarray)
endfor

Populate(N, i, nnarray):
    while N != 0
        Choose a random number between 1 and k, call it nn
        for attr <- 1 to numattrs
            Compute: dif = Sample[nnarray[nn]][attr] − Sample[i][attr]
            Compute: gap = random number between 0 and 1
            Synthetic[newindex][attr] = Sample[i][attr] + gap ∗ dif
        endfor
        newindex++
        N = N − 1
    endwhile
    return
</syntaxhighlight>

where

* <code>N</code> is the amount of SMOTE, where the amount of SMOTE is assumed to be a multiple of one hundred
* <code>T</code> is the number of minority class samples
* <code>k</code> is the number of nearest neighbors
* <code>Populate()</code> is the generating function for new synthetic minority samples

If <code>N</code> is less than 100%, the minority class samples will be randomized, as only a random subset of them will have SMOTE applied to them.

== Implementations ==
Since the introduction of the SMOTE method, there have been a number of software implementations:
* imbalanced-learn
* smote_variants: implementation of 86 SMOTE variations
* ImbalancedLearningRegression
